Turn in all of your notes and event materials when you have completed the event.
situation:
You are a twenty-three-year-old dental laboratory technician who supports a fifteen-year-old sibling on a single income. The judge is a counselor at NORTHGATE FAMILY CREDIT COUNSELING, a non-profit agency. You carry $19,400 in student loans, and your credit score of 610 has already raised the cost of the credit you are offered.

Your goal has been a $4,000 emergency fund. Your sibling needs braces, and the orthodontist wants $1,800 down. DEBTCLEAR SOLUTIONS, a for-profit firm, advertises a lower monthly student loan payment for a $900 enrollment fee. NORTHGATE would set up the same repayment plan for $35 a month and no enrollment fee.

Your paycheck also carries a disability insurance election. Minimum coverage costs $11 a month and replaces a third of your income; full coverage costs $34 a month and replaces two thirds. You are the only earner your sibling has. A CASHWAY EXPRESS storefront nearby offers payday advances against a paycheck.

The counselor (judge) has asked you to recommend a repayment plan and a coverage level. You could pay the $1,800 down for your sibling's braces now, which empties the emergency fund and leaves CASHWAY EXPRESS payday advances as the only place to turn in a bad month. You could keep the emergency fund and full coverage at $34 a month, which delays the braces by a year.

The counselor (judge) will greet you and ask to hear your ideas, and will thank you after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are a counselor at NORTHGATE FAMILY CREDIT COUNSELING. Business background is the same as the situation above.

You have asked the technician to recommend how to handle the $19,400 in student loans — through NORTHGATE at $35 a month or through DEBTCLEAR SOLUTIONS for a $900 enrollment fee — what disability coverage level to elect, and whether the $1,800 down payment for the braces happens now or waits.

During the presentation you are to ask the participant the following questions:
judgeQuestions: How would you explain this decision to your sibling?
If your sibling disagreed with the choice, what would you change?
